steps.title: The start screen
steps.text: Craft opens on the start screen. A whole experiment — plates, drugs, doses, cell lines — is easiest with the wizard. "Open protocol" reads any .tdd file saved by D300e Control.

steps.title: How an experiment goes
steps.text: The five stages: design here, prepare the plates and tubes, print on the D300e, read the plates, then paste the values back here for viability and synergy.

steps.title: Start the wizard
steps.text: Click "New experiment". This example: Bortezomib × Venetoclax on two myeloma cell lines, 384-well plates.

steps.title: Plate and well volume
steps.text: Pick the plate type and the volume already in each well (medium + cells): 50 µL here. Doses are calculated against this volume.

steps.title: DMSO limit
steps.text: The most DMSO a well may receive, as % of the well volume. Craft warns you when a dose would need more.

steps.title: Replicate plates
steps.text: How many identical plates to print of each layout: 2.

steps.title: Priming wells and diluted stocks
steps.text: Keep these ticked. Very low doses then come from a second, diluted tube of the same drug (D300e "fluid shift / extend"), and tiny drops are primed in border wells first.

steps.title: Your plate, drawn
steps.text: The picture follows every change. Shaded wells are the PBS border: you fill them by hand, the D300e does not print there.

steps.title: Next
steps.text: Next: the drugs.

steps.title: First drug and its stock
steps.text: Name each drug and the concentration of the tube you will pipette into the dispense head: Bortezomib, 10 mM in DMSO.

steps.title: Second drug
steps.text: Venetoclax, also 10 mM in DMSO. "Add drug" adds more; each extra drug can pair with the first one on its own set of plates.

steps.title: Next
steps.text: Next: the doses and where they go.

steps.title: Highest and lowest dose
steps.text: Bortezomib runs across the columns. Type the highest dose (10 µM), the lowest (0.0001 µM = 0.1 nM) and the number of doses (10): the dilution step is calculated for you.

steps.title: Units per drug
steps.text: Prefer nanomolar for this drug? Change its unit: the doses are converted (10 µM becomes 10000 nM) and every table and map shows nM. The file for the D300e is unchanged.

steps.title: Second drug down the rows
steps.text: Venetoclax runs down the rows: from 3 µM in 1:2 steps, 6 doses, one row each. "Add 0" adds the single-drug and vehicle-control wells.

steps.title: Dose strip: which tube each dose comes from
steps.text: Each circle is one dose. Solid = from the stock; striped = from the diluted stock "Bortezomib - 1:30" that Craft added because 0.1 nM needs less than one drop of 10 mM.

steps.title: What you will need
steps.text: The right side always shows plate 1 as it will look, how many plates to print, and which cassettes and dispense heads you need with which solution. If a layout does not fit, it says how many plates or heads it would take.

steps.title: Next
steps.text: Next: the cells.

steps.title: Cell lines and arrangement
steps.text: Two cell lines, one in the top half and one in the bottom half of each plate. Cell lines are not sent to the D300e; they label every well in the results.

steps.title: Randomize within each cell line
steps.text: Tick to print the doses in a random order, against edge and gradient effects. A well only trades places with wells of the same cell line, so you still seed the cells as drawn.

steps.title: Next
steps.text: Next: review.

steps.title: Review
steps.text: The review lists every plate and the bench steps that follow. Nothing is changed until you press Create.

steps.title: Create the plates
steps.text: Create: the plates open in the editor. One Undo takes the whole wizard back.

steps.title: The plate map
steps.text: Plate 1 as the D300e will print it. Colour = drug; a well with two drugs is split. The list on the left holds the drugs, cell lines and plates.

steps.title: Randomized: as printed or as planned
steps.text: This plate is randomized. "As printed" shows where each dose really lands; "As planned" shows the tidy layout you designed (and is where you edit). "De-randomize" removes the shuffle.

steps.title: Doses view
steps.text: In the planned view, "Doses" draws each drug as a gradient: pale = lowest, dark = highest. Easy to see that the series runs the right way.

steps.title: Cell lines view
steps.text: "Cell lines" shows where to seed which cells: MM.1S on top, KMS-11 below.

steps.title: Any well, explained
steps.text: Click a well: the panel below the map lists its drugs, concentrations, DMSO and where it is printed.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: The Check tab lists anything the D300e would refuse or warn about — doses below one drop, too much DMSO, wells over the volume — in plain words with the wells to look at.

steps.title: Run tab
steps.text: Run: which cassettes you need and what to pipette into each dispense head.

steps.title: The cassette drawing
steps.text: Pipette the bold volume into each head, left to right. Each head shows the solution and its concentration; striped heads hold the diluted stock. Click to enlarge or save it for the bench.

steps.title: Save the protocol
steps.text: Save writes the .tdd for D300e Control and an experiment file next to it (cell lines, units, results). Copy both to the D300e computer, open the .tdd there and press Run.

steps.title: After the read-out
steps.text: After incubation and the plate read (e.g. CellTiter-Glo), open the Results tab of the same file.

steps.title: Paste the plate reader values
steps.text: Copy the plate from the reader's Excel sheet and paste it here; row and column labels are fine. (This demo uses simulated values.)

steps.title: Read them in
steps.text: "Use for plate 1" matches every value to its well — on a randomized plate, to the well the dose was really printed in.

steps.title: Heat map and synergy
steps.text: The map now shows the signal. Below: viability and Bliss synergy per cell line (red = the pair kills more than expected). The SynergyFinder package adds ZIP, HSA and Loewe in R.

steps.title: Excel
steps.text: Export Excel: one row per well with cell line, every drug's concentration, DMSO, raw signal and % of vehicle, plus replicate statistics. That is the whole cycle.
